miniProject.title: Cached generation, proved and measured
miniProject.brief: Add a KV cache to the decoder and prove that it changes nothing but cost. Then measure prefill and decode separately, and explain the numbers with the arithmetic from section 4.
steps: Add a per-layer cache of unexpanded K and V to your model, with absolute positions for RoPE, and a forward that takes new tokens, the cache and a start position.

Prove equivalence: greedy tokens match and per-step logits agree within tolerance with the uncached model for MHA, GQA and MQA, chunked prefill, a one-token prompt, a variable-length batch with padding, a sequence that stops early at EOS, and a reused cache slot.
Derive the KV-cache bytes for your config and for one published model config, and check the formula against the real tensor sizes of your cache.
Measure time to first token and inter-token latency on a CPU or a free GPU across two context lengths and two batch sizes, with warm-up, device synchronization and repeated trials.
Explain the measurements: which phase is compute-bound, which is memory-bound, and how the cache changes the cost of each decode step.
Connect the atlas lab adapters for section 5 and pass tests/test_s5_kv_cache.py.
deliverables: The cached model and its equivalence test suite.
A KV memory sheet: the formula, your config, one published config and the measured cache size.
A latency report: time to first token and inter-token latency per regime, the timing method, and an explanation of each trend.

checks.name: Atlas lab, section 5: cache equivalence, cache size and decode cost
checks.note: Run in labs/llm-foundations of an ai-atlas clone after you connect adapters.py to your package. It compares cached and uncached logits and tokens across head layouts, offsets and chunked prefill, checks the cache-size formula against your cache, and fails a decode step that recomputes the prefix.

rubric.pass: Cached and uncached greedy tokens match on the lab cases.
rubric.strong: Per-step logits also match within 1e-5 on your own adversarial cases, and a deliberately wrong RoPE offset makes your tests fail.

rubric.pass: The KV formula matches the measured cache size.
rubric.strong: The sheet scales the formula to a published model at long context and large batch, and names what dominates memory there.

rubric.pass: Prefill and decode are timed separately with warm-up and repeated trials.
rubric.strong: The report gives medians with spread, synchronizes the device and states what the timings exclude.

rubric.pass: Each trend is explained in a sentence.
rubric.strong: The explanation uses arithmetic intensity from section 4 and predicts one result before measuring it.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone artifact 3: the cached-generation half of the dossier and the full-prefix cache equivalence that the stage milestone asks for.
